steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two cookie sheets.

Beat butter and 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar in a bowl using an electric mixer until smooth. Stir in vanilla. Combine flour, salt, and 1/2 teaspoon of cinnamon; stir into butter mixture to form a stiff dough. Shape dough into 1-inch balls.
Mix 1 cup confectioners' sugar and 1 teaspoon cinnamon together in a shallow bowl. Roll balls in cinnamon mixture to coat; transfer cookies to prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until nicely browned, about 15 to 20 minutes. Cool cookies on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Polvorones de Canele (Cinnamon Cookies)
raw_recipe.description: Polvorones are a shortbread-style Mexican cookie. This recipe adds cinnamon to the dough and rolls the cookies in cinnamon sugar for a delicious treat.

review.reviewBody:
I loved these as posted, then I made some changes to try to duplicate the real Spanish version of these delightful cookies, but many will probably be turned off by the LARD.

Substitute lard for the butter, double the cinnamon in the cookie, and roll in sesame seeds instead of the sugar/cinnamon coating. They should come out super soft like fine sand and just hold together. In Spain they are traditionally wrapped after baking and you SQUEEZE the cookie before unwrapping so it holds together. Forget Chocolate Chip or Peanut Butter Cookies, THIS IS WHAT COOKIES ARE ALL ABOUT!

These are tasty. In my experience, cinnamon flavor is often lost in baking, and my brother loves cinnamon, so I increased the amount in the batter to 1 TABLESPOON. Also, figured out that these are similar to Mexican Wedding cookies, so i let the cookies cool and rolled them in the cinnamon (much more than recipe) and confectioner sugar AFTER baking. Now to see what he thinks! Addendum: chilled dough in fridge overnight

The first try with this recipe, I was really underwhelmed by the lack of cinnamon coming through once the cookies cooled. It was more like butter sugar cookies, which I'm not a big fan of.

On the second try, I increased the cinnamon in the batter to about 1 1/2 teaspoons, and the vanilla to about a table spoon. For the powdered sugar, I upped the cinnamon to 1 1/2 teaspoons and made sure not to dust off too much of the sugar coating before placing it on my baking sheet to give it more of a crunch once they've cooled. 

These turned out very delicious, not too much cinnamon, but just enough to actually taste it rather than the buttery confectioner's sugar taste (bleh). And this is coming from someone who's not a fan of sugar cookie-esque recipes. lol

These cookies are truly luscious! I doubled the recipe and mixed them in my KitchenAide. Easy. I didn't add extra cinnamon to the cookie dough and I "eye-balled" the cinnamon/sugar rolling mixture, dumping in what looked like the right amt. of cinnamon. I did roll them again in the cin/sugar as soon as them came out of the oven. I used a one Tablespoon scoop and baked them at 350 in my convection oven for 15 minutes. Oh, I put half the dough in the freezer while I scooped out the first batch. Not a good idea! The dough congealed very quickly and I had to let it soften a bit in order to scoop it again. No harm done, however! I really had no problem with "soft" dough. Make these!

these are very good, will definitely be on my Christmas list next year! I doubled the vanilla and cinnamon in the cookies, next time use 1 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 cup icing sugar for rolling, 1 tbsp scoop made 37 cookies, 15 minutes was perfect, tossed cookies in leftover sugar and cinnamon mixture.

I made a few changes AFTER I made the recipe as directed. The recipe is perfect as is, and the changes I made are for personal preferences only. Here is as I made: oven 350, 1 cup butter + 1/2 cup sifted powdered sugar, cream together. Next add 1 tsp vanilla, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp finely grained salt NOT Kosher, as it does not melt well. Finally 1 + 1/2 cup sifted cake flour + another 3 TPS of sifted cake flour. Mix in a separate bowel 1 cup non sifted powdered sugar + 2 tsp cinnamon. Flour counter with some of the powder sugar/cinnamon mix. Roll dough out, using however much powder sugar/cinnamon mix to roll out the dough. Cut with round cookie cutter no more than three inches. Redip cookies into powder sugar/cinnamon mix to recoat the cut cookies on both sides. Place on lined cookie sheet. 15 minutes is usually enough, however oven times vary.

Needed a Mexican cookie for a cookout. These were outstanding! I did as others suggested. Doubled the cinnamon and vanilla in the recipe. After I baked them, I rolled them one more time in the powdered sugar and cinnamon mix. They just melt in your mouth. Big thumbs up!

I have to say these things melt in your mouth. I did take ideas from others and doubled the cinnamon (instead of 1/2 I put 1 tsp of cinnamon). Another thing I also changed was that instead of rolling the ball of dough in the sugar/cinnamon mixture, I baked them first. After they were done cooling, I rolled then in the sugar/cinnamon mixture.

EXCELLENT! The family gobbled them up quickly. My picky kiddo said they were the best cookies she'd ever eaten! I didn't have any issues with dry dough like some reviews mentioned- in fact my dough was a little on the wet side, so I ended up letting it chill for 30 minutes before shaping it. The dough was easy to work with. After rolling the dough in the powdered sugar mixture I returned to the fridge for another 10 minutes or so before baking. After removing from the oven I was little disappointed by how little powdered sugar I could see on the outside so I rolled each of them in the extra powdered sugar mixture (there was plenty) while they were still warm and then allowed to cool. Definitely a keeper!

I followed the recipe as written except I increased the cinnamon to 1 Tbs. and the vanilla to 1 1/2 tsp. I combined sanding sugar and cinnamon and rolled the cookies before baking and again after baking and cooling. These were melt in your mouth cookie goodness. You can't eat just one! A new family favorite.

I also tweaked this recipe slightly, and was very happy with the results: I doubled the recipe amounts for a larger yield, and also added an extra 1/4 cup more powdered sugar, 1/3 cup more flour, and 1/2 tsp more vanilla for the dough, as well as quadrupling the amount of cinnamon for the dough (baking mellows out cinnamon enormously). Cinnamon sugar powder: I only needed about a cup of powdered sugar and I put quadruple amount of cinnamon for that as well, sifting the sugar and cinnamon together. When you bake them, it melts the sugar and cinnamon coating, providing a very thin sweet coating to a light buttery cookie. Be careful if you make small, truly 1 inch diameter balls, the bottoms can caramelize and burn quickly. (caramelization is okay, burning is not, but burning quickly follows caramelization). Please keep in mind that the extra amounts of sugar, flour and cinnamon I added are for a doubled recipe of 48 yield. Delicious! I'm going to make these for christmas gifts when that time of year comes around...

Easy recipe and very similar to a Dutch Teacake recipe I inherited. As suggested I doubled the cinnamon in the cookies. After baking I dusted the cookies with more of the sugar/cinnamon blend - yummy!
Delicious, BUT the dough needs to be refrigerated prior to baking!

They are not exactly like the Mexican cookies that the Abuela used to get but they taste wonderful. Like other reviews I read, you don’t need that much powdered sugar to roll in and it bakes into the cookies so you don’t see any sugar on the cookies. My ‘s cookies used granulated sugar and cinnamon (with lots of cinnamon). I might try that next time. I dusted with more powdered sugar just to help them look more appetizing. Easy to make and yummy!
Everyone loved these and it was very budget friendly!
Easy to make, taste great. Can't wait to make them again. I made them for a friend from Ecuador I hope she likes them.
Light, airy, puffs of sugar and cinnamon. What's not to love?
Very good big hit with family. I did let the dough balls rest in refrigerator for 25 minutes before rolling in the powder.

I love this. The cookies are always a blast. My brother eats them all unless I tell him not to. These are super easy to make and are scrumptious. I only do 1/2 cup of sugar for when you roll the balls.

Can’t figure it out. Followed recipe to the letter but result is a very powdery, crumbly cookie. Almost like sand. I could tell the consistency wasn’t right when we made the dough but pressed on anyway. Back to the drawing board…:-(
